title: Wajdi and the River That Argued
logline: Wajdi fights Sabri until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Wajdi, who carried the ecstasy of finding, standing beyond the self, ran headlong against Sabri, who was quiet knowing. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Wajdi noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Wajdi had fought so hard in Sabri was only the part of Wajdi that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
